title: ScreenTrustCAD at Capio Sankt Göran Hospital, Stockholm: Lunit Insight MMG as a third reader leads to 19 more screen-detected breast cancers than two radiologists
summary: At Capio Sankt Göran Hospital, Lunit's Insight MMG read 55,581 mammograms beside two radiologists; the three together found 269 cancers against 250 by the radiologists alone.
account: Karolinska Institutet researchers ran the ScreenTrustCAD study at Capio Sankt Göran Hospital in Stockholm, Sweden, from 1 April 2021 to 9 June 2022. Lunit's Insight MMG, version 1.1.6, read every screening mammogram in the background as an independent reader beside the usual two radiologists. If any of the three readers flagged an examination, it went to a consensus discussion, where two radiologists saw the AI score and the marked area and decided whether to recall the woman. Among 55,581 women aged 40 to 74, the two radiologists alone would have found 250 cancers. With the AI as a third reader, 269 cancers were found, a relative proportion of 1.08. The study also showed that one radiologist plus AI was non-inferior to two radiologists, with 261 cancers against 250. The study was paired, so every woman was read by every strategy, and it ran at one hospital with one mammography vendor. Lunit was one of the funders; the paper states that the funders had no role in the study.
purpose: Insight MMG was built to detect breast cancer on mammograms. In ScreenTrustCAD it served as an independent reader; the extra cancers found were that purpose.
deployer: Capio Sankt Göran Hospital with Karolinska Institutet (ScreenTrustCAD study)

ratings.reason: Nineteen women had breast cancer found at screening only because the AI flagged their examinations (269 cancers with AI against 250 without).

ai_role.statement: In a paired design, every examination was read by two radiologists and by the AI, and the authors counted the cancers found by each reader combination, so the cancers that only the AI flagged are attributable to it.
